title: Liao Dynasty
capsule: The Liao dynasty was founded by the Khitan leader Abaoji (Emperor Taizu), who proclaimed himself khan in 907 and emperor in 916; the dataset attests it from 911 to 1125. At its apex in the late tenth century the Liao controlled Manchuria, Mongolia, and the Sixteen Prefectures of northern China ceded by the Later Jin in 938, and extracted annual silver and silk payments from the Song dynasty under the Chanyuan Treaty of 1005. The Liao operated a sophisticated dual administration, with separate Chinese and Khitan bureaucratic systems, and patronized both Buddhism and indigenous Khitan script. The Jurchen Jin dynasty overthrew Liao in 1125, capturing Emperor Tianzuo; a remnant fled westward to establish the Qara Khitai khanate in Central Asia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Liao territorial extent is well-documented through Chinese dynastic histories (Liaoshi), stele inscriptions, and treaty texts; the Sixteen Prefectures boundary with Song China is particularly precise, while northeastern and northwestern steppe frontiers are less sharply defined.
